phase_name: Packaging decision gate -- measure the trimmed checker

objectives.description: Record the baseline from research for comparison
Set supportInterpreter=false for check_certificate only, rebuild, re-measure
Re-run the capability handshake against the trimmed binary
Decide and record the packaging route based on the measurement
Restore the flag in the companion repository and note the finding

baseline_measured_live.note: Matches research report's recorded baseline (313,863,000 / 219,351,032 / 69,143,681) to within gzip metadata/version noise.

findings.decision: Out-of-band opt-in artifact remains the recommendation; in-wheel shipping (Route A) is declined on the measured number. supportInterpreter=false shrinks the gzip-9 artifact from ~65.9MiB to ~32.8MiB (roughly halved), but 32.8MiB is still in the tens of MiB, not single-digit -- the threshold Phase 6's own decision rule names for in-wheel plausibility. This does not change Phase 1-5's recommendation (Route B: documented opt-in via BIMODAL_CHECKER_BIN plus optional SHA-256 pinning), which stands alone and blocked on nothing here.
findings.companion_repo_state: lakefile.toml restored to HEAD (git diff clean); .lake/build/bin/check_certificate rebuilt back to the exact baseline size (313863000 bytes) so no build artifact is left in the trimmed state either.
